insights.title: What Prosperify just verified on this deal
insights.intro: Four questions actually asked in the demo above, across the six documents of the Asteria / NimbusCore file. Every gap is recalculated and cited from source, never summarized from memory — this is what a lawyer would otherwise spend hours, and six open documents, establishing by hand.
insights.footnote: Pick "try another prompt" in the demo above to replay each of these questions.
insights.cta: Replay these scenarios with your own contracts

items.question: Summarize the key terms of this deal and tell me what's still open before signature.
items.finding: The contract binds Asteria Retail and NimbusCore for €3.24M over 36 months, 420 stores, with automatic renewal every 12 months. But five clauses remain open: termination for convenience is one-sided after 12 months, the liability cap is 12 months of fees, the SLA commits to only 99.5% availability, and the incident notice runs from confirmation rather than discovery. None of these five clauses match Asteria's internal standard.
items.highlight: Five clauses remain open before signature, none aligned with the internal standard.

items.question: Compare the final package to our contract policy and rank the gaps by priority.
items.finding: Three gaps touch structural protections and are top priority: the liability cap (€1.08M against a €2.16M policy minimum), one-sided termination, and the incident notice (72 hours from confirmation against 24 hours from discovery — two different starting points, not just two different durations). Two gaps are secondary: the 99.5% SLA and the 30-day non-renewal notice.
items.highlight: Three top-priority gaps touch structural protections: cap, termination, incident notice.

items.question: Do the documents contradict each other on service level and security?
items.finding: Yes, on two fronts. The order form shows 99.9% as a "contractual target," while the SLA — the only document that defines the measurement method — commits to only 99.5%, and the negotiation note wrongly states this is "resolved." On security, the DPA runs the incident notice from confirmation (72 hours) while internal policy requires 24 hours from discovery. The MSA's precedence order doesn't settle which availability figure applies.
items.highlight: Two documented contradictions need to be resolved before signature.

items.question: Prepare a negotiation briefing for Legal with the wording to obtain.
items.finding: Verdict: not ready to sign. Five priority wordings to obtain — raise the cap to 24 months of fees with reciprocal carve-outs, open termination for convenience to both parties with matching notice, move the incident notice to 24 hours from discovery. In addition: a firm 99.9% SLA and a 60-day non-renewal notice. Follow-up, not a blocker: post-contract data retention, left "to confirm" in the DPA.
items.highlight: Verdict: NOT READY TO SIGN until three priority wordings are obtained.

criteria.title: What a reliable answer must guarantee, in legal
criteria.intro: On contractual commitments, the priority order isn't the same as for generic use.

items.title: Risk detection before signature
items.description: A lawyer who manually cross-checks an MSA, a contract policy and an SLA typically needs several hours to spot an open clause or a contradiction like the ones above. Prosperify takes the question in plain language and cross-checks the documents in seconds, before the contract is signed on an incomplete basis. The gain isn't just time: it's the ability to detect the risk before it becomes contractual.

items.title: Accuracy of the cited clause
items.description: A general-purpose model paraphrases a plausible, well-drafted clause, sometimes one the contract doesn't contain. Prosperify only cites what it finds written in the document, at the right version — the redline under negotiation, not an outdated draft. That's the difference between a plausible clause and a defensible one.

items.title: Defensible traceability
items.description: Every claim in the answer links back to the document, page and clause that supports it, and a click opens the PDF at the exact highlighted passage. In a dispute or a review, the lawyer no longer has to hunt down the clause by hand: it's already there, ready to be shown as-is.

On a corpus that holds confidential contracts and negotiation notes, these questions aren't secondary — they decide the go/no-go, often before the quality of the answers does.

items.question: Reconstruct this patient's journey and summarize the key clinical information.
items.finding: History: hypertension and permanent atrial fibrillation, amoxicillin allergy documented in 2019, four active medications before hospitalization. Estimated GFR moves from 68 in September 2025 to 44 on June 18, 2026, with a mismatched automated "stable" comment. Dehydration episode from June 23-25, eGFR 46 on admission then 52 at discharge, with a lab follow-up expected within 7 days.
items.highlight: eGFR drops from 68 to 44 over 9 months, with an automated comment that doesn't reflect it.

items.question: Which record inconsistencies need to be verified during medication reconciliation?
items.finding: Three points to verify, none resolvable from the file alone: the amoxicillin allergy, documented in primary care, shown as "none known" in the discharge summary; the rivaroxaban dose — 20mg on the prescription and discharge list, 15mg in the cardiology letter; the creatinine/potassium check requested within 7 days, missing from the record as of July 10. None of these sources settles which value is correct.
items.highlight: Three documented discrepancies, none resolvable from the file alone.

items.question: Show the trend in renal function and the documents that explain each step.
items.finding: Estimated GFR at 68 mL/min/1.73m² in September 2025, then 44 on June 18, 2026, 46 on admission June 23 and 52 at discharge June 25 — a partial improvement during hospitalization, with no measurement available after discharge. The automated "stable" comment attached to the June 18 result is inconsistent with this drop from 68 to 44.
items.highlight: The automated "stable" comment is inconsistent with the drop from 68 to 44.

items.question: Prepare a review sheet for the follow-up visit, without giving medical advice.
items.finding: Three checks before the follow-up visit: confirm and correct the amoxicillin allergy status, contradicted at discharge; establish the rivaroxaban dose actually prescribed and taken, between 20mg on the prescription and 15mg in the cardiology letter; retrieve or reschedule the creatinine/potassium check requested for July 2. No treatment change is proposed here — validation by a healthcare professional required.
items.highlight: Three points flagged for review — no clinical decision is proposed.

items.question: Summarize YTD performance and explain the paradox between growth and cash.
items.finding: Revenue at €12.4M (+24%), EBITDA at €1.1M: on the P&L alone, the business looks healthy, and a first glance would stop there. But cash falls by €2.2M over the period, a drop driven entirely by operations. Cross-checking the P&L against the cash-flow detail narrows the gap to a single cause: rising receivables, with no anomaly elsewhere in working capital.
items.highlight: Rising receivables alone explain the entire cash decline.

items.question: Compare actuals to budget and flag the variance that deserves board attention.
items.finding: Revenue beats budget by €0.6M: on that metric alone, the quarter looks like a win. But cash is €1.4M short, a gap proportionally larger than the EBITDA miss. The cause shows up in the collection period, 78 days against a 49-day budget, tying up €1.52M more than planned — a figure neither document states on its own.
items.highlight: The 78-day collection period ties up €1.52M more than budgeted.

items.question: Which receivables explain the risk, and do the invoices confirm the aging report?
items.finding: Two accounts, MetroFleet (€1.20M, 62 days overdue) and NordTransit (€0.75M, disputed), account for 47.6% of receivables on their own. The source invoices, recalculated line by line, reconcile to the cent with the aging report: the delay isn't a data-entry error, it's a real collection issue, with a distinct, documented cause for each account.
items.highlight: Two accounts already account for 47.6% of total receivables.

items.question: Challenge the CFO note and prepare three sourced closing actions.
items.finding: The note to the board calls the cash tension "mostly seasonal." The structural collection gap, 78 versus 49 budgeted days, contradicts that: it isn't a calendar effect, it's a drift that persists. The NordTransit dispute, worth €0.75M, isn't even mentioned in the note — exactly the kind of blind spot a cross-checked reading surfaces before the committee, not during it.
items.highlight: The structural DSO contradicts the note's "seasonal" diagnosis.

criteria.title: What a reliable answer must guarantee, in finance
criteria.intro: On numbers that go to the board, the priority order isn't the same as for generic use.

items.title: Speed of detection
items.description: A controller who manually cross-checks a P&L, a cash-flow statement and an aging report typically needs several hours to spot a gap like the ones above, and only if they know where to look. Prosperify takes the question in plain language and cross-checks the documents in seconds, before the gap reaches the board already softened into a cleaner story. The gain isn't just time: it's the ability to challenge a narrative before it becomes the official version.

items.title: Accuracy of the figures
items.description: A general-purpose model paraphrases and rounds; on a P&L or an aging report, rounding is enough to make the gap that matters disappear. Prosperify recalculates every amount from the source documents — 1.20 + 0.75 = 1.95M, checkable line by line — and never states a figure it hasn't found written in the corpus. That's the difference between a plausible answer and one that holds up in front of an audit committee.

items.title: Full traceability
items.description: Every claim in the answer links back to the document, page and sentence that supports it, and a click opens the PDF at the exact highlighted passage. In a review or an audit, the controller no longer has to hunt down the source by hand: it's already there, ready to be shown as-is.

integration.title: What your IT team will check before signing off
integration.intro: A CFO can be convinced by the demo above. IT looks at something else: where the documents live, who can access them, what happens if the vendor changes policy, and how long the integration will actually take. On a corpus that holds closing accounts, client invoices and internal notes bound for the board, these questions aren't secondary — they decide the go/no-go, often before the quality of the answers does.
integration.cta: Talk to an engineer before the technical committee

items.title: Integration with what you already have
items.description: Prosperify doesn't replace your ERP or your DMS: it reads on top of them, with connectors to the repositories your finance team already uses (data room, file shares, accounting exports) and authentication aligned with your identity provider via SSO (OIDC or SAML). No re-entry, no extra document repository to maintain.

items.title: Isolation and encryption
items.description: Each client gets a siloed instance, with no shared indexing across organizations. Documents are encrypted at rest and in transit, and depending on the deployment model, keys can stay under your control. Your documents are never used to train a general model: they're queried within your perimeter, full stop.

items.title: Operational traceability
items.description: Every access, every query and every document opened is logged. In a security review or an internal audit, your security team has a full trail to present, not a promise to take on faith.

items.title: Reversibility
items.description: Your documents and indexes stay exportable at any time. If you switch tools down the line, you leave with your data and your conversation history, not with a proprietary silo you have to negotiate to get back.

faq.subtitle: Key answers about sources, security, deployment and document governance with Prosperify.

items.question: Does the AI continuously learn from my data?
items.answer: No. Client corpora are not used to train general models. They are used to generate sourced answers inside the agreed project perimeter.

items.question: Where are documents hosted?
items.answer: It depends on the selected model: dedicated cloud, hybrid architecture or local deployment. The trust perimeter is defined with the client around security, confidentiality and operational constraints.

items.question: Does Prosperify replace experts?
items.answer: No. Prosperify helps automate document search, synthesis, extraction and comparison. Decisions, validation and interpretation remain with business experts.

items.question: How are answers verified?
items.answer: Answers are generated from selected document excerpts and linked back to the sources used. Insufficiently supported statements can be surfaced to support human review.

items.question: Can access be limited by role, store or corpus?
items.answer: Yes. Access can be governed by role, store, corpus, user or confidentiality level. Out-of-scope operations are refused according to configured rules.

items.question: Do we need to rebuild the information system?
items.answer: No. Prosperify can be added as a document intelligence layer on top of existing systems. Integration can start with one corpus, one store and one business use case before expanding.

items.question: Which formats are supported?
items.answer: Prosperify is designed for structured and unstructured documents, including PDF, Word, Excel, CSV, JSON and other business corpora depending on project scope.

items.question: Which deployment modes are possible?
items.answer: Three approaches are possible: dedicated cloud, hybrid or local. The choice depends on confidentiality level, infrastructure constraints and sovereignty needs.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body: Privacy is a condition of our business: Prosperify processes confidential document corpora on behalf of its clients. Prosperify is committed to complying with French and European data protection law, in particular Regulation (EU) 2016/679 of 27 April 2016 (the "GDPR") and the French Data Protection Act of 6 January 1978 as amended.
items: Data you entrust to us as a client stays within the deployment perimeter you choose: dedicated cloud, hybrid, or an installation on your own infrastructure.
Client corpora are not used to train general-purpose models.

This policy covers the prosperify.app website and our commercial exchanges. Processing of the documents you entrust to us under a contract is governed by the data processing agreement annexed to that contract.

sections.title: 1. Definitions
sections.body: Capitalised terms have the meaning given by Article 4 of the GDPR. In particular: "Personal data" means any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person; "Processing" means any operation performed on such data; "Controller" means the party determining the purposes and means of processing; "Processor" means the party processing data on behalf of the controller.

sections.title: 2. What is the purpose of this policy?
sections.body: This policy describes how Prosperify collects, uses and protects your personal data. It applies to:
items: visitors to prosperify.app and its sub-pages (blog, team, job openings);
people who contact us through the contact form or request a demo;
candidates applying to a job opening;
contacts at our clients, prospects and partners.

sections.title: 3. What is Prosperify's role regarding your data?
sections.body: Prosperify's role depends on the processing at hand, and the distinction matters:
items: For data collected through the website, prospecting and the commercial relationship, Prosperify acts as controller: it determines the purposes and the means.

For the documents and data you upload to the platform under a contract, Prosperify acts as processor: it acts only on the client's instructions, under the terms of the data processing agreement. The client remains the controller of its corpus.

sections.title: 4. How does Prosperify collect your data?
sections.body: Your data comes from three sources.
items: Directly from you: contact form (name, email address, optional phone number, subject and message content), demo request, job application, exchanges by email, phone or at professional events.

From third parties or public sources: professional contact details from public sources or business databases, in the context of business-to-business prospecting, as well as introductions made by our partners.
Automatically as you browse: connection and browsing data collected through cookies and trackers subject to your consent. No non-essential tracker is set before you make your choice in the banner.

sections.title: 5. What does Prosperify do with your data?
sections.body: Each processing activity serves a purpose, relies on a legal basis and has a defined retention period.

sections.title: 6. Who does Prosperify share your data with?
sections.body: Your data is accessible to the Prosperify teams that need it, within the limits of their duties, and to the following recipients:
items: Hosting: the website and its services are hosted by [À COMPLÉTER] (provider, country of establishment and server location). Client deployments follow the perimeter set out in the contract.
Processors: the providers listed in Annex 1 act on our behalf, on our instructions, under a contract compliant with Article 28 of the GDPR.
Authorities: Prosperify may disclose data to a public or judicial authority where a legal obligation requires it.

Transfers outside the European Union: where a provider is located outside the EU in a country without an adequacy decision, the transfer is governed by the European Commission's standard contractual clauses or another safeguard under Articles 46 and 49 of the GDPR.

sections.title: 7. What are your rights over your data?
sections.body: Under the GDPR and the Act of 6 January 1978, you have the following rights:
items: Right of access (Art. 15): obtain confirmation that your data is processed and receive a copy of it.
Right to rectification (Art. 16) and erasure (Art. 17): have your data corrected or deleted.
Right to restriction of processing (Art. 18): where you contest the accuracy of the data, consider the processing unlawful, or need it to establish or defend legal claims.
Right to data portability (Art. 20): retrieve the data you provided, in a structured format, where processing is based on consent or on a contract.
Right to object (Art. 21): object at any time to direct marketing, and to processing based on our legitimate interest.
Right to withdraw your consent at any time, without affecting the lawfulness of processing carried out beforehand.
Right to give directions on what happens to your data after your death.
Right to lodge a complaint with the CNIL: www.cnil.fr/en/plaintes.

sections.title: 8. How does Prosperify protect your data?
sections.body: Prosperify implements the appropriate technical and organisational measures required by Article 32 of the GDPR, considering the risks of destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorised disclosure or unauthorised access.
items: Encryption of data in transit and at rest.
Access separation by role, team and document store, with logging of consultations.
Isolation of client environments according to the chosen deployment mode.
Security reviews and incident handling, with notification to the CNIL and to data subjects in the cases set out in Articles 33 and 34 of the GDPR.

sections.title: 9. What about cookies?
sections.body: On your first visit, a banner lets you accept or refuse non-essential trackers. Refusing is as easy as accepting and does not prevent you from browsing the site. Only cookies strictly necessary for the site to work are set without your agreement. Your choice is stored for 6 months and can be changed at any time from the banner. Audience measurement trackers have a maximum lifetime of 13 months.

sections.title: 10. What about social networks and third-party sites?
sections.body: The site links to external sites, in particular LinkedIn. Clicking those links redirects you to those services: Prosperify then collects no data about that visit. Information gathered by those platforms is governed by their own privacy policies and by the settings you have defined there. Prosperify is not responsible for the content or the practices of those sites.

sections.title: 11. Who can use Prosperify?
sections.body: Prosperify's services are intended for professionals acting in the course of their business, of legal age and able to enter into contracts. The site is not intended for minors and Prosperify does not knowingly collect data about them. If you believe a minor has sent us data, write to us and it will be deleted.

sections.title: 12. How does this policy apply?
sections.body: Prosperify may amend this policy to reflect legal, regulatory or technical developments. In the event of a substantial change affecting the purposes, the data collected, the exercise of your rights or transfers, you will be informed in writing at least fifteen (15) days before it takes effect. The version online on the date of your visit is the one that applies.

sections.title: 13. How to contact Prosperify
sections.body: To exercise your rights or for any question about this policy, write to us. To handle your request, we may need to verify your identity.
items: Controller: [À COMPLÉTER] (company name, legal form, registered address, company number).
Data protection contact: [À COMPLÉTER] (dedicated email address, and the details of the data protection officer if one has been appointed).
Response time: one month from receipt of the request, extendable by two months where the request is complex.

sections.title: 1. Purpose and scope
sections.body: These terms govern access to prosperify.app and the use of the Prosperify services. They apply to every visitor of the site and every user of the services. Professional use of the platform is further governed by a contract between Prosperify and the client organisation: in the event of conflict, that contract prevails over these terms.

sections.title: 2. Definitions
sections.body: In these terms:
items: "Services" means the website, the Prosperify platform and the related features.
"Client" means the organisation that has entered into a contract with Prosperify.
"User" means the individual accessing the Services, on their own behalf or on behalf of a Client.
"Corpus" means the documents and data a Client uploads or connects to the platform.
"Answer" means the output produced by the agent from the Corpus, together with its citations.

sections.title: 3. Acceptance and changes
sections.body: Accessing the Services constitutes acceptance of these terms. Prosperify may amend them to reflect legal, regulatory or functional developments. In the event of a substantial change, affected Users are informed in writing at least fifteen (15) days before it takes effect. The applicable version is the one online on the date of access.

sections.title: 4. Description of the Services
sections.body: Prosperify provides a document intelligence solution for querying internal corpora and obtaining answers tied to their sources. The Services include:
items: search combining semantics, keywords, document context and visual signals;
answers citing the passages used, with a reference back to document and page;
access management by role, team and document store;
distinct deployment modes: dedicated cloud, hybrid, or installation on the Client's infrastructure.

sections.title: 5. Access, accounts and security
sections.body: The Services are reserved for professionals of legal age able to enter into contracts. Credentials are personal and confidential: the User is responsible for actions taken from their account and must inform Prosperify without delay of any unauthorised use. The Client administers its own Users' rights and remains responsible for the perimeter it opens to them.

sections.title: 6. User obligations
sections.body: Users undertake to use the Services for their intended purpose and in compliance with applicable law. The following are prohibited:
items: uploading unlawful content, or documents for which the User does not hold the necessary rights;
any attempt at unauthorised access, circumvention of security measures or degradation of the service;
large-scale automated extraction of the site or platform, and reverse engineering of the Services;
reselling, providing or sharing access outside the perimeter set out in the contract.

sections.title: 7. Client Corpus and data
sections.body: The Client retains full ownership of its Corpus. Prosperify acquires no rights over those documents and holds only a limited, non-exclusive licence strictly necessary to provide the Services, for the term of the contract. Client Corpora are not used to train general-purpose models. At the end of the contract, data is deleted or returned as set out in the contract and the data processing agreement.

sections.title: 8. Prosperify intellectual property
sections.body: The Services, their software components, documentation, trademarks and graphical elements are protected and remain the exclusive property of Prosperify or its licensors. The contract grants a personal, non-exclusive and non-transferable right of use, limited to the agreed term and scope. No other transfer of rights is granted.

sections.title: 9. Nature of the answers produced
sections.body: Answers are produced from the Client's Corpus and are meant to be verified. They stay tied to the excerpts used precisely so that verification is possible.
items: Answers do not constitute legal advice, medical advice or investment recommendations.
They do not replace the judgment of a qualified professional, who must review the cited passages before any binding use.
Prosperify does not warrant the completeness of an incomplete Corpus, nor the accuracy of the documents provided to it.

sections.title: 10. Availability and maintenance
sections.body: Prosperify uses reasonable efforts to keep the Services available. Interruptions may occur for maintenance, updates or in the event of an incident. Service level commitments, where they exist, are defined in the contract. [À COMPLÉTER] (state the applicable availability commitments and maintenance windows).

sections.title: 11. Pricing, orders and payment
sections.body: Professional access to the Services is subject to a fee, set out in a quote or purchase order. [À COMPLÉTER] (state billing frequency, payment terms, late payment penalties and renewal conditions). Browsing the site and its public content remains free.

sections.title: 12. Term, suspension and termination
sections.body: The term of the contract and its renewal and termination conditions are set out in the contract. Prosperify may suspend access in the event of a serious breach of these terms, an established security risk or non-payment, after a formal notice has remained without effect except in a justified emergency. Termination does not affect obligations arising before it takes effect.

sections.title: 13. Warranties and limitation of liability
sections.body: Prosperify is bound by an obligation of means in providing the Services. Its liability may only be engaged for proven fault and for direct damage only. Indirect damage, loss of opportunity, loss of data attributable to the Client's failure to back up, and the consequences of use inconsistent with these terms or of a decision taken without verifying the cited passages are excluded. [À COMPLÉTER] (state the liability cap set out in the contract). No clause limits liability in cases of wilful misconduct, gross negligence or personal injury.

sections.title: 14. Personal data protection
sections.body: The processing of personal data is described in the data protection policy. Where Prosperify processes data on behalf of a Client, a data processing agreement compliant with Article 28 of the GDPR is annexed to the contract and sets out the instructions, the security measures and the fate of the data at the end of the relationship.

sections.title: 15. Force majeure
sections.body: Neither party may be held liable for a failure resulting from force majeure within the meaning of Article 1218 of the French Civil Code and French case law. The affected party informs the other without delay. If the impediment lasts more than thirty (30) days, either party may terminate the contract without compensation.

sections.title: 16. Governing law and jurisdiction
sections.body: These terms are governed by French law. Failing an amicable resolution within thirty (30) days from notification of the dispute, it shall be brought before the competent courts of [À COMPLÉTER] (chosen jurisdiction), including where there are multiple defendants or third-party proceedings.

sections.title: 1. Our approach
sections.body: Prosperify processes confidential corpora: compliance is not paperwork added afterwards, it shapes how the product is built. This page sets out the commitments we make to our clients and to data subjects. It complements the data protection policy, which describes the processing for which Prosperify is the controller.

sections.title: 2. Allocation of roles
sections.body: The qualification changes with the processing activity, and determines who decides what:
items: Controller: Prosperify, for website, prospecting and commercial relationship data.
Processor: Prosperify, for documents and data processed in the platform on behalf of a client, on that client's instructions only.
Controller: the client, for its corpus, its users and the purposes it pursues.

sections.title: 3. Data processing agreement
sections.body: An agreement compliant with Article 28 of the GDPR is annexed to every client contract. It sets out in particular:
items: the subject matter, duration, nature and purpose of the processing, and the categories of data and data subjects;
the obligation to act on the client's documented instructions, including for transfers;
the confidentiality undertaking of the persons authorised to process the data;
the security measures implemented under Article 32;
the conditions for engaging sub-processors and the client's prior information;
assistance to the client for data subject requests, impact assessments and breach notifications;
the fate of the data at the end of the contract: deletion or return, at the client's choice.

sections.title: 4. Your rights and how to exercise them
sections.body: Everyone has the rights of access, rectification, erasure, restriction, portability and objection, as well as the right to withdraw consent and to give post-mortem directions. Where the request concerns data processed on behalf of a client, it must be addressed to that client as controller: Prosperify assists them in responding within the deadlines. Requests received directly are forwarded to the client concerned without delay.
items: Response time: one month from receipt, extendable by two months for complex requests.
Contact: [À COMPLÉTER] (dedicated data protection email address).
Complaint: you may refer the matter to the CNIL at any time, www.cnil.fr/en/plaintes.

sections.title: 5. Record of processing activities
sections.body: Prosperify maintains the record required by Article 30 of the GDPR, both for the processing for which it is the controller and for processing carried out on behalf of its clients. A relevant extract may be provided to a client for its own compliance obligations, upon written request.

sections.title: 6. Sub-processors
sections.body: Engaging a sub-processor is subject to the client's authorisation under the terms of the data processing agreement, and to prior information in case of addition or replacement, leaving the client time to raise a reasoned objection. Each sub-processor is bound by obligations equivalent to those of Prosperify. The list of sub-processors is annexed to the data protection policy.

sections.title: 7. Transfers outside the European Union
sections.body: Prosperify favours processing and storage within the European Union. Where a transfer to a third country is necessary and that country does not benefit from an adequacy decision, the transfer is governed by the European Commission's standard contractual clauses, supplemented where appropriate by additional measures following an assessment of the local legal context. In dedicated or on-premise deployments, the geographic perimeter is set in the contract.

sections.title: 8. Security measures
sections.body: The following measures are implemented under Article 32 of the GDPR:
items: encryption of data in transit and at rest;
access management by role, team and document store, with logging of consultations;
isolation of client environments, up to a dedicated instance or an installation on the client's infrastructure;
regular backups and tested restoration procedures;
code and configuration reviews, and vulnerability management;
team awareness training and contractual confidentiality undertakings.
[À COMPLÉTER] (add the certifications or audits actually held: ISO 27001, SOC 2, HDS, penetration tests. State nothing that is not currently valid.)

sections.title: 9. Personal data breaches
sections.body: In the event of a personal data breach, Prosperify notifies the client concerned without undue delay after becoming aware of it, with the information needed for the client's own notification to the supervisory authority within the 72-hour deadline set by Article 33. Where Prosperify is the controller, it notifies the CNIL itself and, where the risk is high, informs data subjects in accordance with Article 34.

sections.title: 10. Retention and deletion
sections.body: Retention periods for the processing for which Prosperify is the controller are set out in the data protection policy. For data processed on behalf of a client, the period is the one the client sets. At the end of the contract, data is deleted or returned at the client's choice, within the agreed period, including in backups according to their rotation cycle.

sections.title: 11. Impact assessments
sections.body: Where processing is likely to result in a high risk, the client carries out a data protection impact assessment under Article 35. Prosperify provides the necessary technical information: architecture, data flows, security measures, location and sub-processors.

sections.title: 12. Location and sovereignty
sections.body: The deployment mode determines the data perimeter. In a dedicated cloud, the instance is isolated and its location is set in the contract. In hybrid mode, sensitive processing stays within the client's perimeter. In an on-premise deployment, documents and processing never leave the client's infrastructure. In every case, client corpora are not used to train general-purpose models.

sections.title: 13. Contact
sections.body: For any question about compliance, the data processing agreement or the exercise of your rights: [À COMPLÉTER] (dedicated email address, and the details of the data protection officer if one has been appointed). You may also contact the CNIL, 3 place de Fontenoy, 75007 Paris, www.cnil.fr.
